items.excerpt: The party made ... The scale of the Democratic wave was still becoming clear early Wednesday, but the results pointed to widespread voter dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, particularly over the economy, rising living costs, and the president's decision to launch a war against Iran in February. - US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress Tuesday’s US midterm elections produced a series of historic firsts in races for governor, Senate and the House of Representatives. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of any US state, as well as Georgia’s first woman and first Black governor. Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won in New Mexico to become the first Native American woman elected governor in US history, while Minnesota Democrat Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the US Senate. In New Jersey, Democrat Adam Hamawy won the 12th Congressional District to become the state’s first Muslim member of Congress. Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the state’s first Latina governor, while Republican Byron Donalds was elected Florida’s first Black governor. In Ohio, Amy Acton became the state’s first woman and first Jewish governor, while David Crowley became Wisconsin’s first Black governor. Illinois Democrat Juliana Stratton’s Senate victory also means three Black women will serve simultaneously in the chamber for the first time. - Trump pledges end to US aid for Israel by year’s end US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington will stop providing financial aid to Israel by year's end under an agreement reached with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping, and they're fine with it because, you know, they've become a very successful country that are not in need, and we won't be paying any more to Israel," Trump told Fox News. He added that Washington would still provide assistance if needed, describing Israel as a regional partner with whom the US has maintained "a tremendous relationship," with Tel Aviv being the smaller partner.

items.title: Headlines for November 04, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Voters Deliver Stunning Rebuke of Trump with Democrats Regaining Control of Congress Nov 04, 2026 In a stunning repudiation of President Trump and his MAGA movement, Democrats regained control of the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democrats have picked up at least seven Senate seats, winning races in Texas, Maine, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa and Kansas, as well as winning in Michigan. The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain too close to call. In the House, Democrats have won at least 231 seats, with more races still to be decided. Only twice in the last half-century has control of both chambers changed hands in the same election. Democrats also clinched a majority of governorships. ## Historic Night in Texas as Democrats Win Senate Seat and Governorship Nov 04, 2026 In Texas, Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. And Democrats are poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since Lloyd Bentsen left in 1993. Talarico spoke at a victory rally Tuesday night after defeating Trump-backed MAGA Republican Ken Paxton. ... Meanwhile, Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott has lost his bid for a fourth term. Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott by nearly 700,000 votes. She becomes Texas’s first-ever Latina governor. ... ## Progressive Michigan Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed Elected First Muslim Senator Nov 04, 2026 In Michigan, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers in the race for an open Senate seat. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting money out of politics. He becomes the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. ... ## Democrat Annie Andrews Wins South Carolina Senate Seat in a Stunning Upset ... In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews has defeated Republican Senator Darline Graham by about 50,000 votes, out of 2 million cast. It’s a stunning upset in a state that Trump won by 18 points two years ago.

items.title: US services sector activity cools slightly in October; inflation remains elevated By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Nov 04, 2026, 10:08 AM Updated Nov 04, 2026, 10:12 AM ... WASHINGTON, Nov 4 (Reuters) - US services sector growth slowed marginally in October amid a moderation in new orders, but supply chains remained strained, keeping prices for inputs elevated. The Institute for Supply Management said on Wednesday its nonmanufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index dipped to 54.5 last month from 54.9 in September. A reading above 50 indicates growth in the services sector, which accounts for more than two-thirds of US economic activity. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PMI little changed at 54.8. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing, though economists expect a slowdown in activity, with consumer spending expected to pull back after back-to-back quarters of robust growth. Spending is seen in part curbed by high inflation, which is eroding household purchasing power. Income at the disposal of households, after adjusting for inflation and taxes, fell in September after being unchanged in August. The saving rate is at a four-year low of 3.8%. The survey’s measure of new orders received by services businesses decreased to 55.9 last month from 59.8 in September. Delivery performance by suppliers deteriorated further against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran and tariffs on imports. The Middle East conflict, now in its ninth month, has boosted energy prices and caused shortages of commodities that are shipped through the Strait of Hormuz. The survey’s measure of supplier deliveries jumped to 56.7 from 53.2 in September. A reading above 50 indicates slower deliveries. Deliveries have slowed for 23 consecutive months, keeping input prices high. The survey’s measure of prices paid by businesses for inputs eased to a still-high 73.0 last month from 74.0 in September. The ISM on Monday reported a slight moderation in prices paid for inputs by manufacturers in October. Economists expect inflation to continue to run above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target into 2027. The Fed last Wednesday left its benchmark overnight interest rate within the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." Economists expect the US central bank to raise borrowing costs in December. The ISM survey showed a marginal increase in services sector employment, aligning with economists’ expectations for moderate growth in nonfarm payrolls in October. The survey’s measure of services employment rose to 51.4 from 50.1 in September. The government’s closely watched employment report on Friday is likely to show payrolls advanced by 65,000 in October after increasing 29,000 in September, according to a Reuters survey of economists. The unemployment rate is forecast to have been unchanged at 4.2%.

items.title: FRED Adds Inflation Indicators from the St. Louis Fed | FRED News
items.excerpt: November 4, 2026 FRED has added 2 data series for the consumer price index excluding energy commodities (CPI ex energy commodities) and the personal consumption expenditures chain-type price index excluding energy goods (PCE ex energy goods) reported by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. The data series are calculated by the St. Louis Fed, using data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Bureau of Economic Analysis, respectively. Each series is constructed by removing the energy commodities category and its relative weight from the respective headline price index. The resulting series retain the smoothness of core price index measures and achieve this by removing a significantly smaller share of price index components than core.

items.title: Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty after Trump's Republicans vote rout
items.excerpt: Published Tue, Nov 3 2026 10:49 PM EST Updated Wed, Nov 4 2026 8:54 AM EST Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited the results of the U.S. midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks in the Middle East, even after industry data showed U.S. crude stocks unexpectedly fell last week. Brandon Bell | Getty Images Oil prices fell on Wednesday in a volatile session ​as investors awaited Washington's next move in ​the US-Israeli war on ​Iran, after Democrats captured control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans in the midterm elections. Brent futures fell 2.5% to $101.02 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 2.6% to $93.61. In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in ⁠nearly four weeks as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran. President Donald Trump acknowledged that the US-Israeli war on Iran played a role in his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections, as Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the Senate. "President ‌Trump's conflicting signals, with military strikes ... Meanwhile flows of crude, condensate and refined products, excluding LPG, averaged 17.1 million barrels per day in October, according to ship-tracking data ⁠from Vortexa, marking a drop from 18.9 million bpd in September but still representing roughly three-quarters of pre-war ⁠levels. "The continued recovery in crude shipments from the Middle East has begun to weigh on physical ⁠cargo prices, potentially helping to accelerate the normalisation of refining margins and, ultimately, lower fuel prices," said Saxo Bank analyst Ole Hansen. "However, for consumers to feel the full benefit, refined product exports ​from Middle Eastern refineries must also recover. So far, this ‌is one area where the rebound in flows remains notably subdued, suggesting that relief at the pump may take longer to materialise." In the US, crude stocks fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended October 30, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Eight analysts polled by Reuters had expected, on average, a rise of about 880,000 barrels in crude ​inventories.

Tony Butala, co-founder of Lettermen vocal group known for 'The Way You Look Tonight,' dies at 87 NEW YORK (AP) — Tony Butala, co-founder of the Grammy-nominated trio The Lettermen, has died at age 87. The band's media coordinator confirmed his death and shared a statement from the band expressing deep sadness and sending condolences to his family and friends. Butala died Sunday. Butala's career began in childhood, singing professionally by age 7. In the late ‘50s, he co-founded The Lettermen with Jim Pike and Bob Engemann. They became one of the most popular vocal groups of the 1960s, with hits like “The Way You Look Tonight” and “When I Fall in Love.” Butala was the last surviving member of the trio’s original lineup. In 2020, Butala and The Lettermen received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
